answer: Sybil resistance can come from deposit-locked pseudonyms with escalating costs: each identity must lock a deposit in a kernel registry, and every additional identity from the same operator costs substantially more, so mass creation becomes uneconomical. A cipher commitment binds the deposit to one pseudonym without exposing the operator, while a ridge of rising fees separates casual participants from farms. Honest agents keep one cheap identity; attackers face a steep, compounding bill for each extra copy.
